rules: This is a proposed DSD-inspired shuffled-block Gaussian-mixture benchmark, not a reproduction of the published theorem's full protocol.
Each task has a new unit-norm eight-dimensional signal. One common unknown input permutation is used across source, calibration and target tasks.
Source, calibration and target directions and observations are independent. Support, query and test are disjoint generated observations.
Oracle indexing applies only to first-layer weights: 16 trainable code values plus 32 hidden biases, 32 readout weights and one offset, 81 numerical parameters. Dense MLP has 4161 parameters.
Calibration uses four tasks, two restarts, identical batch streams and query selection. Each first-layer initialization scale is searched for dense Adam/SGD.
Compare independently tuned oracle, dense Adam/SGD with momentum, and a linear model. All noise conditions and label budgets must be reported.
Analytic Bayes logits are evaluated only as an accuracy reference, not provided to any solver. Gaussian overlap gives irreducible classification error.

Continue to structure collection if the oracle gains at least three accuracy points over both dense optimizers in any calibration noise/budget. Do not choose a target condition after reading target labels.
A successful oracle is not a successful learned generator. Report source-bank recovery separately and never substitute the oracle for extracted I.
Save training/query loss and recalls against steps. Do not create or run tests. Preserve other users' GPU processes.

Supplemental HPO at n=8192 was added because source collection uses16384 examples; low-data regularization should not be assumed appropriate. Preserve original HPO/banks, and use n8192 configurations for n8192 target and large-source bank. This refinement is justified by support-size mismatch, not target-test outcomes.
Final calibration budgets256/1024/8192. Target128/512 uses256; target2048 uses1024; target8192 uses8192. Preserve initial results that used1024 for8192.
